open_points.subject: OWNER_SESSION_COOKIE_ATTRIBUTES
open_points.question: What exact cookie attributes does this newly named constant contain, including Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite, Path, Domain, persistence or expiry, and are the same attributes required when replacing or clearing the cookie?
options: Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Path=/; no Domain; no persistent expiry
Secure and HttpOnly only, leaving browser defaults for the other attributes
Different attribute sets for setting and clearing the cookie
open_points.default_guess: Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Path=/; no Domain; a session cookie, with an identical scope when clearing it

witness.initial: The owner signs in successfully through HTTPS and receives a session cookie.
events: module:owner_interface sets the cookie using the newly introduced attributes
The owner follows a cross-site link back to an owner change route or signs out and later revisits the interface
outcomes: With SameSite=Strict and matching clear attributes, the browser withholds the cookie cross-site and removes it on sign-out
With browser-default SameSite or a mismatched Path or Domain on clearing, the browser may send the cookie cross-site or retain it after sign-out

set_aside.subject: owner session cookie origin confinement
set_aside.question: How must the cookie be confined to Registry's origin when standard browser cookies are scoped by host and path, not by port, so cookie attributes cannot prevent transmission to another origin on the same host?
options: Give the owner interface a dedicated hostname and make the cookie host-only
Weaken the obligation from origin-only to host-only
Require every other same-host HTTPS surface to use a path outside the cookie's Path scope
Use a different browser authentication mechanism that can be bound to an origin
set_aside.default_guess: Give the owner interface a dedicated hostname, use a host-only __Host- cookie with Secure and Path=/, and state that origin-only means that dedicated host

witness.initial: The owner interface is at https://registry.example:8443 and another HTTPS service is admissibly listening at https://registry.example:9443.
events: module:owner_interface signs the owner in and sets a host-only session cookie
The browser requests the other service on the same host and different port
outcomes: Following the stated origin-only obligation, the browser does not send the Registry session cookie to port 9443
Following standard cookie behavior, the browser sends the cookie because cookie matching ignores the port
witness.observer: the other same-host service and anyone inspecting that request
